subject: Science
title: Soft and hard
objectives: Children will touch and describe soft and hard objects.
Children will describe rough and smooth with support.
content: Touching soft and hard objects, and describing rough and smooth.
teachingActivities: Let children touch with hands and say each word as they touch; use a mystery bag; never force a child to touch something they dislike; offer a tool instead.
learnerActivities: Touch objects, say soft, hard, rough or smooth and sort objects.
resources: Cotton wool, a sponge, a teddy
A stone, a wooden block, a spoon
Sandpaper, a rough mat, a smooth tile and a leaf
assessment: Observe whether each child says soft or hard for an object and sorts objects with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says soft or hard for a familiar object.
Sorts objects into soft and hard with support.

lessons.title: Touching soft things
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will touch soft things and say the word soft.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use their eyes and ears to explore and name what they see and hear.
resources: Cotton wool, a sponge, a teddy and a soft cloth
lessons.starter: Stroke the teddy and say "Soft, soft, soft." Ask "Can you feel it?"
teacherActivities: Pass the soft objects round and say "Soft" as each child touches.
Squeeze the sponge and the teddy and show how they change.
Close your eyes and feel an object. Ask "Is it soft?"
Put soft things on a tray and name each.
learnerActivities: Children touch each object and say soft.
Children squeeze and say soft.
Child feels an object and nods or says soft.
Child names a soft object.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pass the soft objects round and say "Soft" as each child touches. Children: Children touch each object and say soft.
Step 2. Teacher: Squeeze the sponge and the teddy and show how they change. Children: Children squeeze and say soft.
Step 3. Teacher: Close your eyes and feel an object. Ask "Is it soft?" Children: Child feels an object and nods or says soft.
Step 4. Teacher: Put soft things on a tray and name each. Children: Child names a soft object.

practical.title: Soft things
steps: Put soft objects on a tray.
practical.safety: Use clean items that cannot be swallowed. Watch that no child puts cotton wool in the mouth or nose.

differentiation.support: Stroke the object with the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another soft thing in the room.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the soft things in a basket and say "Soft."
lessons.homeConnection: Find soft things at home, such as a pillow, and say soft.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "touch soft things and say the word soft" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Soft, soft, soft. Teddy is soft.

lessons.title: Touching hard things
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will touch hard things and say the word hard.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use their eyes and ears to explore and name what they see and hear.
lessons.starter: Tap the wooden block on the table and say "Hard." Ask "Is it hard or soft?"
teacherActivities: Pass the hard objects round and say "Hard" as each child touches.
Tap objects on the table and listen to the sound.
Show a soft and a hard object together and ask which is hard.
Let each child choose a hard thing and show a friend.
learnerActivities: Children touch each and say hard.
Children tap and listen.
Child points to the hard object.
Child shows the object and says hard.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pass the hard objects round and say "Hard" as each child touches. Children: Children touch each and say hard.
Step 2. Teacher: Tap objects on the table and listen to the sound. Children: Children tap and listen.
Step 3. Teacher: Show a soft and a hard object together and ask which is hard. Children: Child points to the hard object.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a hard thing and show a friend. Children: Child shows the object and says hard.

practical.title: Hard things
steps: Put hard objects on a tray.
Each child touches and taps them.
practical.safety: Use stones larger than a child’s fist and smooth wood without splinters. Supervise closely and keep objects out of mouths.

differentiation.support: Tap the object together and say hard.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a hard thing outside.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the hard things back and say "Hard."
lessons.homeConnection: Find hard things at home, such as a table, and say hard.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "touch hard things and say the word hard" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Rough and smooth
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will feel rough and smooth surfaces and use the words.
successCriteria: Says rough or smooth with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use their eyes and ears to explore and name what they see and hear.
lessons.starter: Rub the sandpaper and say "Rough." Rub the tile and say "Smooth." Ask "Which is smooth?"
teacherActivities: Pass the rough and smooth objects round and say each word.
Ask "Is it rough or smooth?" for each object.
Put one object in the bag and let a child feel it.
Let each child find a rough and a smooth thing in the room.
learnerActivities: Children touch and say the word.
Child says rough or smooth.
Child feels and says rough or smooth.
Child finds and touches objects.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pass the rough and smooth objects round and say each word. Children: Children touch and say the word.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Is it rough or smooth?" for each object. Children: Child says rough or smooth.
Step 3. Teacher: Put one object in the bag and let a child feel it. Children: Child feels and says rough or smooth.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child find a rough and a smooth thing in the room. Children: Child finds and touches objects.

practical.title: Rough and smooth
steps: Put rough and smooth objects on the table.
practical.safety: Use fine sandpaper only and watch that no child rubs it hard or near the face. Wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Guide the child’s finger across the surface and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a rough and a smooth thing on the playground.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names rough and smooth with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects back and say "Rough and smooth."
lessons.homeConnection: Feel rough and smooth things at home, such as a wall and a plate.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "feel rough and smooth surfaces and use the words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sort soft and hard
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort objects into soft and hard.
successCriteria: Puts a soft object in the soft basket
Puts a hard object in the hard basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use their eyes and ears to explore and name what they see and hear.
resources: Two baskets labelled soft and hard
Six objects: three soft, three hard
lessons.starter: Show two baskets and say "One is for soft things and one is for hard things."
teacherActivities: Pick up a teddy, feel it and put it in the soft basket.
Pick up a stone, feel it and put it in the hard basket.
Let each child pick an object, feel it and choose a basket.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say soft.
Children watch and say hard.
Child feels and sorts the object.
Children touch and say soft or hard.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up a teddy, feel it and put it in the soft basket. Children: Children watch and say soft.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick up a stone, feel it and put it in the hard basket. Children: Children watch and say hard.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick an object, feel it and choose a basket. Children: Child feels and sorts the object.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each basket together. Children: Children touch and say soft or hard.

practical.title: Soft and hard baskets
steps: Put six objects on the mat.
Put it in the right basket.
practical.safety: Use large objects that cannot be swallowed. Supervise sorting and turns.

differentiation.support: Use two objects and feel them together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find one more soft and one more hard thing.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which basket does the teddy go in?
Which basket does the stone go in?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts soft and hard objects with support
lessons.conclusion: Count the objects in each basket and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort soft and hard toys at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort objects into soft and hard" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 touch check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses touch to describe objects.
successCriteria: Says soft or hard for an object
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use their eyes and ears to explore and name what they see and hear.
lessons.starter: Say "We touch with our hands" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: soft, hard and rough and smooth.
At each station ask "Is it soft or hard?" or "Is it rough or smooth?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: soft, hard and rough and smooth. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Is it soft or hard?" or "Is it rough or smooth?" Children: Child answers with a word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Touch stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use safe objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend the words.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says soft or hard; says rough or smooth; sorts objects.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.homeConnection: Describe things at home as soft, hard, rough or smooth.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses touch to describe objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
